title: Shadow On‑Call Onboarding and Synthetic Incident Lab
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This page defines Redwood's Shadow On‑Call Onboarding program and the Synthetic Incident Lab (SIL). The goal is to accelerate new responders' competency with our operational surface (services, monitoring, runbooks, comms) by combining structured shadow shifts with automated, reproducible incident simulations. This document is a prescriptive playbook: staffing steps, learning milestones, evaluation criteria, sample scenarios, and templates for evidence and customer communications.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: new on‑call engineers, SRE mentors, rotation managers, and engineering managers.
- Scope: applies to service-facing on‑call rotations that support the Redwood API, router, and inference runtime (services named: api-gateway, request-router, inference-core).
- Excludes: product support queues, sales escalation, and business continuity incident response. Those have separate onboarding flows.

Why this exists
----------------
- Past onboarding has been uneven: new responders report long time-to-first-take and inconsistent use of runbooks.
- SIL provides repeatable, observable training that can be replayed for requalification and promotion gates.
- Shadowing plus synthetic scenarios reduces customer risk by keeping novices away from live incident leadership until they meet competency thresholds.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- Reduce average time-to-first-take to < 24 hours after sign-up for new interims.
- 90% of new on‑call engineers should meet "Responder Level 1" within 6 shadow shifts.
- Post‑lab confidence score >= 4.0/5 on the training survey.
- Trackable artifacts: evidence logs, simulation postmortems, trainer signoffs.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- New Responder: complete prework, attend shadow shifts, pass SIL scenarios.
- Mentor (SRE): leads shadow shifts, provides feedback, approves progression.
- Rotation Manager: schedules shadow shifts, ensures runbook freshness is assigned.
- Simulation Engineer (Lab Owner): builds & runs synthetic incidents in the staging environment and records telemetry.
- Oncall Onboarding Coordinator (People-Ops eng liaison): tracks completion and badges in HR system.

Prerequisites (prework checklist)
--------------------------------
1) Access & accounts
   - Verify VPN, SSO, and service-account access to staging cluster: request via internal-iam with tag "oncall-onboard".
   - Ensure PagerDuty and Slack rotation membership.
2) Reading
   - Read: "Responder primer: incident lifecycle at Redwood" (15 min).
   - Read assigned runbooks for api-gateway, request-router, inference-core.
3) Tooling
   - Local setup: kubectl context (staging), access to Grafana dashboards, Kibana logs, and the internal tracing UI.
   - CLI quick commands: see Appendix.
4) Ethics & comms
   - Review Customer Communication Tonebook (link in related_pages).

Shadow shift structure (4‑hour block recommended)
-----------------------------------------------
- 00:00–00:15 — Warm up and expected outcomes: mentor reviews current signals and SLO state.
- 00:15–01:15 — Observational rotation: mentor triages live low-risk alerts while narrating decisions.
- 01:15–02:15 — Guided take: new responder performs triage steps against a non-customer impacting alert with mentor co-pilot.
- 02:15–03:15 — Simulation run (short): run a 20–30 minute SIL micro-scenario with synthetic traffic.
- 03:15–04:00 — Debrief, evidence capture, and action items (runbook updates, playbook gaps).

Synthetic Incident Lab (SIL) overview
------------------------------------
SIL runs in a dedicated staging tenancy to emulate live signals while isolating customer traffic. Each scenario exercises a specific competency dimension: detection, containment, mitigation, rollback, and comms. Simulations are deterministic and recorded for later review.

Sample SIL scenarios (index)
---------------------------
1) KV cache evictions under burst (service: inference-core) — tests cache warm-up strategies and autoscaler behavior.
2) Trailing-slo latency hump (service: request-router) — tests routing fallthrough and temporary capacity bump.
3) API 5xx spike due to dependency (service: api-gateway -> auth-service) — tests dependency isolate/fallback.
4) Noisy neighbor GPU saturation (inference-core pool) — tests tenant isolation, burst policy, and graceful degradation.

Each scenario includes:
- Objective and success criteria (SLO/thresholds)
- Preconfigured telemetry (alerts emulated, dashboards pre-populated)
- Step‑by‑step inject and rollback scripts (bash/python snippets)
- Expected comms timeline and template

Example scenario header (human-readable)
---------------------------------------
Title: API 5xx spike due to auth-service regression
Objective: Identify cause within 10 minutes, enable fallback path within 20 minutes, and restore API success rate to >= 99.0% within 45 minutes.
Success criteria: error-rate<1% sustained, latency P95 within 2x baseline, no customer-facing incident notice required.

Runbook templates and must-have sections
---------------------------------------
Every operational runbook referenced by SIL must contain the following sections:
- Detection signals (alerts with exact query)
- Impact classification (customer-visible, internal-only, severity tiers)
- Quick containment steps (commands, feature flags, API calls)
- Verification checks (metrics and queries)
- Escalation matrix with oncall names and PD severity level thresholds
- Post-incident checklist and evidence capture links

Sample runbook verification table (plaintext)
--------------------------------------------
| Check | Query/Location | Expected result | Owner |
|-------|----------------|-----------------|-------|
| API success-rate | grafana/dashboard/api-slo | >= 99% | responder |
| Error logs | kibana/apigateway/errors | no auth 500 | responder |
| Traces | tracing/ui?service=api-gateway | top 3 traces show auth fallback | mentor |

Escalation matrix (abridged)
---------------------------
1) Severity P0 — Global customer impact, immediate bridge. PD: page primary oncall and SRE lead, notify Eng VP.
2) Severity P1 — Partial loss affecting >20% tenants. PD: page oncall, advise rotation manager within 15m.
3) Severity P2 — Degradation in non-critical function. PD: create alert ticket and page only if >30m unresolved.

Scoring and competency gates
---------------------------
- Each SIL has a rubric with weighted sections: detection (20%), containment (30%), mitigation (30%), comms (20%).
- Level progression:
  - Level 0 (Observer): completed prework.
  - Level 1 (Responder): successful completion of 3 SIL scenarios + 6 shadow shifts.
  - Level 2 (Leader): successful leading of 2 SILs and one live non-P0 incident as secondary.
- Mentor signs off via the onboarding tracker for each gate.

Postmortem and evidence capture workflow (for SIL and live incidents)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Capture timeline: use the incident-evidence form (link) and store logs in evidence-bucket with prefix: /evidence/{incident-id}/.
2) Draft concise timeline within 48 hours and tag the incident with the appropriate service and SLO IDs.
3) Simulation prometheus/grafana snapshots must be archived alongside the postmortem.
4) Include a short learning card (one paragraph) that will populate the training catalog if the responder demonstrated an interesting mitigation pattern.

Customer Communications templates (short forms)
----------------------------------------------
- Initial internal summary (to CS & ENG-safety):
  - "We are investigating elevated 5xxs impacting API calls for a subset of tenants. ETA for next update: 30 minutes. No action required from customers at this time."
- Short customer-facing notice (if customer-impacting):
  - "We are aware of increased errors for some API requests; our team is actively mitigating. We will post updates every 30 minutes until resolved."
- Recovery message:
  - "The incident impacting API calls is resolved. Root cause: regression in auth-service; rollback to v2.14.1 applied at 14:32 UTC. We will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

Onboarding schedule template (4-week plan)
------------------------------------------
Week 0: Prework and tool access
Week 1: Shadow shifts (6 x 4hr) + one SIL micro-scenario
Week 2: SIL full scenarios (3) + runbook quiz
Week 3: Co‑lead simulation and lead one low-risk live incident with mentor
Week 4: Assessment, Level 1 signoff, and badge issuance

Game-day cadence and maintenance
--------------------------------
- Quarterly SIL refresh: Simulation Engineer schedules a refresh every quarter to keep scenarios aligned with recent incidents.
- Runbook rotators: owners must review their runbooks at least once per quarter and after any live incident.
- Badge requalification: Level 1 responders requalify annually via one SIL scenario.

Appendix — CLI snippets and common queries
------------------------------------------
Troubleshooting example: find top 10 sources of 5xx in Kibana (example query):
```
GET /api/logs/_search
{
  "size": 0,
  "aggs": { "top_hosts": { "terms": { "field": "service.name.keyword", "size": 10 }, "aggs": { "top_errors": { "terms": { "field": "error.keyword" } } } }
}
```
Grafana quick verification: open dashboard "API SLOs / Overview" and verify "api_success_rate" panel shows >= 99%.
Sample kubectl command for safe containment (staging only):
```
kubectl -n inference-staging scale deployment inference-core --replicas=0
# wait for verification then scale back
kubectl -n inference-staging scale deployment inference-core --replicas=3
```

Feedback loop and continuous improvement
---------------------------------------
- After each SIL, mentors submit a short retro that is consolidated monthly. Action items are tracked in the Oncall Improvements board.
- New runbook gaps found during SILs are triaged with a 7‑day SLA for hotspot fixes and 30‑day SLA for full runbook rewrites.

-----------------
